title: Racial Inequalities in Maternal Mortality: Population-Based Retrospective Study Using Data from the ReMaP Project
content: Objective: To investigate racial disparities in maternal mortality and access to obstetric care in the state of São Paulo, comparing maternal health outcomes and access to healthcare services between Black (Black and Brown) and White women. Methods: This was a retrospective, cross-sectional, population-based observational epidemiological study conducted using secondary data extracted from the Restructuring and Redesign of the Maternal and Neonatal Care Network (ReMaP) panel, integrated into the Brazilian Obstetric Observatory. A total of 6,781 maternal deaths registered in the state of São Paulo between 2000 and 2025 were analyzed. Variables included race/color, education level, marital status, type of maternal death, period of death, medical care, place of occurrence, and investigation by Maternal Mortality Committees. Descriptive analysis was performed using absolute and relative frequencies, with calculation of 95% confidence intervals. Conclusions: Maternal mortality in São Paulo remains associated with significant social and healthcare inequalities, with a predominance of potentially preventable causes and a high occurrence in the postpartum period. The findings reinforce the need to strengthen epidemiological surveillance, improve obstetric care, and expand strategies aimed at promoting equity in maternal health.
